descriptions: the liṅga in which the world dissolves and from which it arises; being-consciousness-bliss (SSM 6.36–38)
the pedestal is Śakti, the liṅga Paraśiva, the universe their union (SSM 11.32)
the liṅga of light shining in all beings (SSM 6.35)
the ocean of consciousness whose waves are the thirty-six tattvas (SSM 1.3)
the one god among the many household gods (Basava)
the husband who does not die or decay (Akka Mahādēvi)
negations: where neither sun nor moon shines (SSM 12.38)
not the avyakta with Maheśvara as its bearer (SSM 12.37)
relation_to_self: The soul (aṅga) is a part of Śiva through beginningless ignorance and progresses through six stations to union (aikya, sāmarasya); in practice the relation is master and servant, and at union difference is seen to be imagined by māyā.
relation_to_world: The world arises from Śiva and is not different from him, as his Śakti's manifestation and his body (aṣṭamūrti) — neither identical with nor separate from him; for the śaraṇas the moving devotee is his living temple.
caveat: The tradition speaks with two voices: the Pañcācārya strand calls its doctrine Śivādvaita or Śakti-viśiṣṭādvaita and insists that difference is real at the level of practice; the vacana strand names Śiva as a personal lord and as the void and resists Vedāntic framing. Both would reject a reading of the one truth that makes the world, the liṅga or devotion illusory (SSM 10.37–43).

descriptions: Śivādvaita: the non-duality of Śiva taught in agreement with Veda and Vedānta (SSM 3.83–87)
the great liṅga is supreme brahman, the breath the jīva (SSM 12.21–24)
negations: beyond speech and mind, self-luminous, indescribable (SSM 12.21–24)
relation_to_self: Difference of Lord and servant governs worship; non-duality is realized at aikya.
relation_to_world: The world is Śiva-made, arising from and dissolving into the liṅga.
caveat: Would reject any reading that dispenses with worship of the liṅga before realization (SSM 10.37–43).

descriptions: the one god, lord of the meeting rivers (Basava)
the beautiful one without death, decay or form (Akka Mahādēvi)
the void in which liṅga and aṅga are not two (Allama)
negations: not the many gods of pot and winnowing fan (Basava)
relation_to_self: The devotee is servant (dāsōhaṃ), bride and finally one with the liṅga.
relation_to_world: The world is to be lived in through work as worship and sharing; the moving devotee is Śiva's temple.
caveat: Many in this strand reject framing the vacanas' Lord in Vedāntic or Sanskrit-philosophical terms.

descriptions: Śiva worshipped exclusively in the liṅga, with Vedic rites retained
caveat: Skeleton only; the Ārādhya view needs sourcing from Telugu texts.
